full_text:
The great comet blazed across the midnight sky, its long luminous tail sparkling with celestial fire. An old grandmother held her little grandson by the hand, pointing to the heavens: "Look, child! My grandfather showed me this very comet when I was a tiny girl sixty years ago! Remember this night!"

Years rolled by; the grandmother slept in the churchyard, and the boy grew into an old, gray-haired man.

One winter night, the celestial comet returned, blazing across the same starry vault. The old grandfather lifted his own little grandson to the window, pointing with trembling fingers: "Look, child! Behold the glory of the heavens! We mortals pass away, but the wonder of creation endures forever."
moral: Celestial wonders return across centuries, while human generations pass like brief waves in the ocean of time.
